title: SDK Mini Runner and Curated Sample Catalog
author: Marisol Ortega
body:
Overview

This page describes the SDK Mini Runner (a lightweight execution harness) and the Curated Sample Catalog — a structured collection of short, runnable SDK examples intended for developer onboarding, support diagnostics, and reproducible canonical fixes. The goal is to reduce time-to-value for new users, speed root-cause analysis for support, and provide a single source-of-truth for sample quality and telemetry.

Goals
- Provide a 1–2 minute local run experience that demonstrates common API patterns (generation, streaming, embeddings, function calling).
- Ensure every sample is runnable with a single command and emits standardized telemetry for triage.
- Maintain a small, high-quality catalog of categorized samples that map to known support issues and canonical fixes.
- Make adding, reviewing, and releasing samples low-friction for engineers and DX writers.

Audience
- SDK maintainers and contributors
- Developer advocates and technical writers
- Support engineers and Solutions Engineering
- Product teams creating integration examples

What is the SDK Mini Runner?
- Lightweight Python-based harness (<= 150 LOC) and equivalent Node starter that:
  - boots a minimal virtualenv/node environment (optional)
  - sets required environment variables from .env or CLI flags
  - runs a sample script and validates expected outputs (basic assertions)
  - captures and uploads (or prints) standardized telemetry and a short run artifact (trace + token counts)

Core components
1) runner/ (python) or runner-js/ (node)
  - run_sample.py / run-sample.js — entrypoint that normalizes env, sanitizes keys, and executes a sample
2) samples/catalog.yaml — metadata registry for all samples (id, path, description, tags, owner, required_env, expected_assertions, telemetry_profile)
3) templates/ — canonical starter templates (generation, streaming, embeddings, multimodal-stub, function-calling)
4) tooling/diagnostics.sh — helper script used by support to reproduce environment and collect artifacts

Sample catalog metadata (catalog.yaml schema excerpt)
- id: sdk-quick-gen-01
- path: samples/generation/quick-gen.py
- description: "Minimal text generation using Redwood hosted model (streaming optional)."
- owner: devx-team@redwood.ai
- tags: ["generation", "streaming", "quickstart"]
- required_env: ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"]
- expected_assertions: ["response contains 'Hello'"]
- telemetry_profile: "sample-minimal-v1"

Adding a new sample (step-by-step)
1. Author the sample under samples/{category}/ with filename short-dashed (e.g., quick-gen.py). Keep <= 80 lines.
2. Add a short README.md next to the sample that documents intents, input, and expected output.
3. Update samples/catalog.yaml with metadata and set owner to a team alias.
4. Run the Mini Runner locally: python runner/run_sample.py --sample samples/generation/quick-gen.py --smoke
   - Expectation: runner exits 0 and prints "SMOKE PASSED".
5. Create a PR against the repo, add reviewer from owner team, and include a short snippet demonstrating observed output.
6. CI job (sample-smoke-check) will execute the runner in a controlled environment and fail the PR if assertions do not hold.

Template: minimal Python generation sample (in README)
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate("Say hello to the world in one sentence")
assert "hello" in resp.text.lower()
print(resp.text)
```

Telemetry and observability requirements
- Every sample must emit the following fields to the local artifact JSON:
  - sample_id
  - sdk_version
  - model_id
  - duration_ms
  - token_input_count
  - token_output_count
  - error_code (if present)
- The Mini Runner will create artifacts in artifacts/{sample_id}/{timestamp}.json. Support can attach these artifacts to a ticket.
- Telemetry profile names should follow: sample-{category}-{stability}-v{n} (e.g., sample-generation-stable-v1).

Support triage mapping (canonical fixes)
- Common symptom: "intermittent streaming disconnects in Python SDK"
  - Canonical sample: streaming/stream-disconnect-demo.py
  - Debug: capture artifacts, run runner with --trace-stream, validate keepalive and chunk sizes.
  - Fix template: update sample to use client.stream(timeout_ms=45000) and add retry logic.
- Common symptom: "deterministic token delta vs console"
  - Canonical sample: embeddings/token-count-check.py
  - Debug: runner prints token counts; compare to service token meter. If mismatch, file issue to runtime team with attached artifact.

CI and release process for the catalog
- All sample PRs must pass sample-smoke-check in CI. The check runs runner in Linux and macOS matrix, node and python where applicable.
- Weekly smoke sweep: a scheduled job runs the full catalog, failing owners by email if a sample regresses.
- To promote a sample from draft -> stable: owner marks telemetry_profile with "stable" and documents a short release note entry. The sample is then eligible for inclusion in the public docs.

Quality guidance and length limits
- Keep samples focused: 30–80 lines; no external infra dependencies.
- Prefer deterministic assertions rather than fuzzy text checks. Use explicit token counts where possible.
- Mark samples that are flaky with tag "flaky" and add mitigation notes. Support should avoid relying on flaky samples for customer repros.

Ownership and governance
- Owner field in catalog metadata is the primary reviewer and oncall contact for the sample.
- Quarterly catalog review: DX leads schedule a review to prune stale samples and rotate owners.
- Deleting a sample requires an owner-approved PR and a changelog entry.

Support playbook: using the catalog during an incoming ticket
1. Identify symptom and map to tags (e.g., "streaming") or search for sample IDs in the catalog.
2. Ask customer to run the matching sample with the Runner (see Support quick-run CLI snippet below).
3. Request artifacts folder created by runner and attach to the ticket.
4. If artifact shows a runtime issue (errors, token mismatch), escalate to eng-serving-runtime with artifact and minimal repro steps.

Support quick-run CLI snippet
```bash
# one-line: sets key and runs a sample, packs artifact
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk.xxx python runner/run_sample.py --sample samples/generation/quick-gen.py --smoke --upload-artifact
```

Maintenance checklist for DX owners (template)
- [ ] Sample runs locally with runner and CI smoke-check.
- [ ] README includes intent, expected outputs, and troubleshooting notes.
- [ ] Telemetry artifact fields present and validated.
- [ ] Tags and owner are accurate in catalog.yaml.
- [ ] No flaky network dependencies.

FAQ
Q: Can a sample call internal-only endpoints?
A: No. Samples must be runnable against hosted public models or a documented stub. If an internal-only flow is required, include a commented stub and mark sample as "internal" with confidentiality set to restricted and add explicit owner_reviewers.

Q: Who reviews sample PRs?
A: The owner listed in catalog.yaml is responsible for the first review. DX lead should be added as secondary reviewer for new categories.
